name: Amazon One Medical
one_liner: Membership primary care from Amazon, by app, video and in some cities in clinics; its doctors treat common anxiety and depression.
best_for: Adults who want a primary care doctor who can also treat mild to moderate anxiety or depression
Prime members who want fast video or message visits
People near a One Medical office who want both in-person and virtual care
People who want medication for common mental health conditions through primary care
not_for: Anyone in crisis: call or text 988, or call 911
People who need ongoing therapy in an area where One Medical doesn't offer it
People with severe or complex conditions who need a psychiatrist (One Medical refers out)
People who don't want an Amazon account
short_description: Amazon's membership primary care: app, video and in-clinic visits; its clinicians treat common anxiety and depression and refer out for therapy.
long_description: One Medical is a US primary care practice owned by Amazon since 2023. Members book same- or next-day visits in the app, by video or message, and in physical offices in a number of metro areas. Its primary care clinicians handle common mental health concerns such as stress, anxiety, panic, sleep problems and depression, including prescribing, and offer longer visits for mental health; they are not psychotherapists. Therapy is available only in select areas, with coaching available more widely, and One Medical refers members to outside therapists and psychiatrists. Membership costs $9 a month or $99 a year for Prime members ($6 a month or $66 a year per added family member) and $199 a year otherwise; visits are billed to insurance. Without a membership, Amazon's pay-per-visit care starts at $29 for a message visit and $49 for a video visit. A separate Mindset behavioral health program is sold to employers. Amazon Health Services is a HIPAA covered entity and says it does not sell patient data.

pricing.notes: Membership covers access; visits are billed to insurance. Added family members $6/month or $66/year with Prime. Pay-per-visit (no membership) from $29 for a message visit or $49 for a video visit. Therapy only in select areas.

privacy.notes: Amazon Health Services is a single HIPAA covered entity; it says it does not sell personal information or PHI and won't use One Medical health data to market other Amazon products without permission. Deletion can be requested, but medical records are kept as law requires. The FTC warned Amazon about patient-data use when the 2023 merger closed (a statement, not a finding).

faqs.q: Is One Medical free for Amazon Prime members?
faqs.a: The $199/year One Medical membership is included free with Amazon Prime. However, actual medical visits still cost your normal insurance copay. The membership provides access and convenience features—insurance covers the care itself.

faqs.q: What mental health services does One Medical offer?
faqs.a: One Medical offers therapy with licensed therapists, mental health medication management through your primary care provider, and referrals to specialists when needed. Services are virtual and in-person depending on your location. It's good for mild to moderate conditions.

faqs.q: Does One Medical accept insurance for mental health visits?
faqs.a: Yes, One Medical accepts most major insurance plans. Mental health visits are billed to insurance like any other medical visit. Your cost is typically your plan's telehealth or specialist copay. Check coverage before your first visit.

faqs.q: Is One Medical good for serious mental health conditions?
faqs.a: One Medical works best for mild to moderate mental health concerns integrated with primary care. For severe depression, bipolar disorder, complex trauma, or conditions requiring specialist psychiatric care, you may need a dedicated mental health provider or specialized program.

primary_uses: Primary care treatment of anxiety and depression, including medication
Same- or next-day video and message visits

patient_summary: You join One Medical ($9 a month or $99 a year with Prime, or $199 a year without) and book video, message or in-office visits with primary care clinicians, who can treat common anxiety, depression, stress and sleep problems and prescribe medication. Therapy is only offered in some areas; otherwise they refer you to therapists and psychiatrists. Visits are billed to your insurance, or you can pay per visit without a membership.

availability.note: Virtual care across the US; in-person offices only in some metro areas; therapy only in select areas.
